config.goal: Port llm.c's fp32 GPT-2 trainer, train_gpt2_fp32.cu, to one SYCL 2020 program, train_gpt2_fp32.cpp, with zero dpct helpers and the model computed on the SYCL device. Start from your own proven port: gpt2_train_proven.cpp in the work dir is the model of this file (forward, backward, AdamW, with oneMath) that you ported earlier. It passed llm.c's own training test on a CPU, an NVIDIA GPU and an AMD GPU, behind a test main. Keep that model code; replace its main with llm.c's real main and host code from train_gpt2_fp32.cu: the same command line (-i -j -o -b -t -l -v -m -s -g), gpt2_build_from_checkpoint on "gpt2_124M.bin", the train and val DataLoaders, the validation loss every -v steps and at the last step, sampling with the tokenizer ("gpt2_tokenizer.bin") every -s steps, and the same printout ('val loss %f' and 'step %4d/%d: train loss %f ...'). Use llm.c's host headers unchanged, as the CUDA file does (#include "llmc/utils.h", "llmc/tokenizer.h", "llmc/dataloader.h"; they are plain C and on the include path). Compile with sources [train_gpt2_fp32.cpp]. A hidden check runs your program on a short tiny-shakespeare run with fixed arguments and compares the losses it prints with llm.c's own trainer (atol 1e-2, llm.c's test tolerance). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources; delete migrate's output (delete_file) once your port is done.

suggestions.types_launch: Use sycl::range<N>/sycl::nd_range<N> directly instead of dpct::dim3 and launch kernels with q.parallel_for.
suggestions.macro: Remove DPCT_* macros (e.g. DPCT_CHECK_ERROR, DPCT_PROFILING_ENABLED) and use plain SYCL.
suggestions.math_intrinsics: Use sycl:: math builtins (sycl::min, sycl::max, sycl::pow, sycl::clamp, sycl::bit_cast) or std:: equivalents in host code.
suggestions.memory_management: Use sycl::malloc_device/malloc_shared + q.memcpy/q.memset + sycl::free(ptr, q). Replace dpct::constant_memory/global_memory with a plain USM allocation or a kernel argument.

For a vendor-portable port call oneMath (UXL Foundation, formerly oneMKL interfaces): #include <oneapi/math.hpp>, oneapi::math::blas::column_major::gemm(q, ...), link -lonemath; it dispatches to MKL, cuBLAS or rocBLAS from the queue's device.
